Encoders count motor rotations in ticks. They report ticks relative to the start - when you turn on the robot (not when you run an OpMode), the zero is reset to whatever position the motor is currently in. This means that if you turn on the robot while, for example, an arm is extended, and you then command the arm to go to tick 0, it will return to that extended position. You can also reset the encoder through code.

getCurrentPosition() returns the current accumulated tick count.

Declare private DcMotor motor.

In init(), get "front_left_motor" from hardwareMap.
In loop(), call motor.getCurrentPosition() and display it with telemetry.addData("Encoder", ticks).

Set power to 0.5 while getCurrentPosition() < 1000, then stop.

This is position-based control. More accurate than timing.
